tips.comment: This is her favourite track, having won 4 times here and never won anywhere else. Was unlucky last time over course and distance, having met trouble in running and is worth backing from the same mark here.
Provided a very dominant victory at Ayr last month. If repeating anywhere near that form, then should easily defy the penalty here.
Burning Cash has only had three runs but won a C5 when second up. He was not disgraced when fifth in listed company last time out and seems on a decent mark for this handicap debut.

This Lightly-raced 3 year old is showing consistent improvement with each race, finishing in 2nd place in 2 consecutive outings, one of which was a handicap at this C&D a week ago. He took the lead before being passed with one furlong remaining, but he rallied back strongly. Given his strong galloping nature, he seems ready to secure his first win.
A well-backed favorite last time at Epsom and disappointed in 4th on his first try over 1m2f. Dropping down in class here and due a win and a better performance with different ground conditions.
Increased in value from foal-yearling-2yo. Makes handicap debut off 68. She has been running with handicaps in mind and could be dangerous from this mark.
Has been threatening to come good soon and has her best chance dropped in grade here, into a 0-68. Worth an each way bet here.

Windsor Pass has just 1 win, that coming at Chelmsford in January off a mark of 56. She has not finished out of the first 5 in her 8 runs since. She must have a good each-way chance again with Jack Dace claiming 7lbs and 4 places on offer.

ORIGINAL THINKER double-entered has run at this venue previously and comes from a yard who have been firing in the winners lately. There has to be a chance this mare surprised connections when winning seemingly unfancied on her seasonal reappearance , so up 4lb may not be a barrier to further success.

Such is the nature of Paul Cole's operation these days, that he is super selective and his turf strike rate is nudging 20% for the last year. This filly makes her handicap debut here off just 65 when 3rd last time out in a novice race. If you watch a replay of that, you'll see that she wasn't knocked about and indeed looked to be staying on nicely in the last half furlong when just encouraged along. This extra furlong will suit and a tongue tie is fitted now. Huggable is the same kind of price and also has an unexposed profile, and they look the likeliest types to upset the more fancied horses. Hopefully, I've sided with the right one.

Looked unlucky in follow-up bid last time, having suffered from positional bias and would have gone close had she come from the same position as those who beat her. Prior to that, showed a good attitude in winning at Redcar. Decent chance in this, nudged up a pound from last time.
Alondra is still a maiden on turf but getting closer. Ran on well late last time to be a closing 2nd. Has run well here before when tackling this minimum trip and was an unlucky loser.
Shaped well LTO and has placed in 3/4 handicaps since the win at Hamilton after a break. This one should be bang there if ready.

Was in good form last summer, but form has dipped. She will need to improve from her last time out effort when only 7th of 8 at Redcar last month. However, she is now 1lb lower than her last winning mark, and going down 2 classes should help.

This looks like a great chance for Raft Up to get another victory on a course he won at two runs back. He had the misfortune to come up against a rejuvenated course specialist at Ripon last time. However, he had the rest comfortably beaten. The trainer is in terrific form, and I would be very hopeful of a very bold show.

Sugar Baby looks like a nice each way play. Form from the last few races is shaping very nicely. Third time lucky, I think, here at this distance. Top weight isn't a worry for me as this horse is pretty consistent with a good jockey. Four places on offer as well.
Won over course and distance on penultimate start. This is tougher up in grade and a 5lb higher mark, but has conditions to suit and didn't pull as hard as usual last time. EW chance.

RIFT VALLEY nowhere near fully exposed as a turf sprint handicapper is a three year old filly taking on her elders. She looks up to yhis company racing now from her career-low mark with plenty more to offer and apparently suited by quick ground she appeals.

Veteran horse who showed some good ability LTO when a credible 4th of 12 at Ripon last month. Also helps that he's a C&D winner but going through a barren run as last win was back in 2023. Current mark provides an opportunity.
Completed a hat trick of wins when winning at Hamilton last month. Up 3 lbs, but that may not be enough to stop making it a 4-timer.

The 5yo should be better for the return five weeks ago on slow ground. Lightly raced last year but a couple of nice runs on quicker ground and nice ratings posted. On a handy mark now and a capable apprentice in the saddle claiming a useful 7lb.

Paying 3 places, I feel 16/1 is good value for lightly raced Reteti. Encouragement on last run at Bath last time, even if slow away, then pulling too hard. That was behind a winner who followed up since. Travelling all the way up from West Sussex.

Slightly improved effort LTO at Ripon last September. He will be looking for improvements, and if he can overcome any potential rustiness, given the long period of inactivity, then I think he can cause an upset, given the same class and going down in distance.

Isle Of Sark started off with a win at Dundalk over seven furlongs for JP O'Brien and has been through numerous trainers including Jamie Osborne without success since then. He is now in his second spell in the UK with A W Carroll, who started him on the flat with four races: three over 12f and the latest over two miles with mixed results, two 2nd places and two last places in small fields. Switching to hurdles, this should get his first hurdles win in a very weak three-horse field.

Won over much further last time around here and was a winner over this trip here the time before. Pedigree suggests that this will be a more adequate trip for him as he goes for the HT under a 7lb penalty, which is negated 5lb by rider's claim. Strong fancy to win this.

The price difference between OVAL STREET and the others does seem rather exaggerated. The nine-year-old is 32lb (27lb with 5lb claim) better off with Keel Strand for 12 lengths over C&D 30 days ago and I certainly didn't think the selection was knocked about in novice company that day. Helen Nelmes' gelding also enjoys an 8lb swing with reopposing rival Stinginhisstep over shorter here in May. Strange things can happen in these small-field affairs and I think Paddy Power's original price of 13/2 was far more like it.

The model I run suggests Shillanavogy can win this one. This model result has been driven by Shillanavogy having the highest RPR of this smaller 5-horse race. Looks well treated off this official ranking and subsequently goes out carrying a middle order amount of weight. Comes here in decent form with solid figures of 1432-1 and looks to add another win to that reliable list. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator largely driven by the lack of value on offer. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Feel The Pinch has won on his last two visits to Newton Abbot. Both were over hurdles, including his win last week, so he does not receive a penalty. However, he was an equally accomplished chaser, and his current mark of 103 is a stone lower than his last winning mark over fences in November 2023.

The model I run suggests Kenmya can win this one. Kenmya lines up here with the highest RPR of this 9-horse race and has an official ranking that leaves Kenmya well treated. Has shown some reasonable form coming into this with a good second-place finish last time out 48 days ago. Race fitness shouldn't be a concern. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4. This has largely been driven by the small gap back to second in the race simulation.

Miss Popalong is a lightly raced 6-year-old who was only below par on one of her last four starts, which came on softer ground. She has shown plenty of ability, including when staying on 3rd at Fontwell over 2m3f in May (form well franked). She was 2nd last time over 3m at Ffos Las on good ground and was well clear of the rest. Today's trip and ground are ideal. She has a winning opportunity here.

Northern trainer Ollie Pears is 2/3 with his runners at Newton Abbot, and Sam Twiston-Davies has 1 winner and 1 second on rides for the yard. So, stats fans will be all over this. A wind-op seems to have made a big difference to the 5-year-old, and front-runners have a good record at this tight track with a short run-in.

The model I run suggests Old Bridge can win this one. Old Bridge lines here with a comparably high RPR but has an official ranking that leaves him bottom in the weights. Goes out carrying 1 stone 5 lbs less than the top weight and current market leader Seeyouinmydreams. Old Bridge has shown some form coming into this with figures of 232-76. Jack Tudor picks up the reins, who's a trusted pair of hands. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4. This is largely driven by the small gap back to second in the race simulation.
After a 9 month absence, this Irish point winner made a strong comeback, having finished 2nd over this C&D last month. He is now poised to enhance the current success of the Evan Williams yard.

JIMMYJEROO remains a low-mileage seven year old running for a classy yard who have been doing well recently through this off-season. This staying chaser arrives in form and race-sharp , so the feeling is connections are turning him around relatively quickly possibly giving off positive signs back home.

The model I run suggests Testflight can win this one. Testflight lines up here with a comparably high RPR to the other 8 runners in the field but has an official ranking that leaves him rock bottom. This subsequently means he goes out carrying over a stone less in weight to most others around this longer 3m 1f trip. That kind of weight difference over this distance could be telling. Last out 10 days ago, so race fitness shouldn't be a concern and has shown some glimpses of form in his figures. 3-U132 and looks to get over the line first again here. Tabitha Worsley picks up the reins and relieves a further 3 lbs claiming. Model has issued a 'low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Janeslittlevoice has plenty of stamina, has won over CD (heavy), and has won on good at Wincanton 3m. The lightly raced 11yo pulled up on return after a 518-day layoff before finishing 2nd here. The next two starts at Fontwell can be forgiven; hampered and lost a shoe and was out of the handicap on penultimate start, before something was amiss last time after travelling well. No major issue as she is back out 10 days later. Those runs would have kept her in good shape for her return here and in a relatively weak event she has big enough claims to make the 20/1 EW value.

Has run at the highest level but has been sent off pushing the pace for stablemate Field of Gold in the Irish 2000 Guineas and St James's Palace. Has some solid form before that and can get running in his own right here in a race that won't take much winning.

Pendragon has had two duff starts since the break but is still two out of two since starting handicapping. The second run was by a bigger margin after taking on weight and eased towards the post. So, he could defy the penalty while stepping up to C4 today, especially if getting a better start.
Staya won a C4 on debut and was not far away when fifth in the Queen Mary at Ascot. She should find today a bit easier.
Colts have the best record in this 5f Listed event. Charlie Appleby has reverted back to 5f for the promising colt, Military Code, who looks sure to go well.

A big step up in class this afternoon, but he looks very open to progress from his recent win at Goodwood over today's 5f trip, which looks like his best. Drawn next to Military Code, which should help him get quickly into his running.
Charlie Appleby has a 40% strike rate with his juvenile debutants at Sandown. This juvenile cost 965,000, so it is clearly highly regarded. I would be surprised to see them get the win here today.
A very interesting looking Novice event with some very well-bred horses on display. John Gosden has sent some very decent animals to compete in these races in the past. A chance is given to Publish.
Term of Endearment is a progressive type, and he faces a few regressive types in this race. I fancy this horse to win today.

Trueshan still won this last year by 2L when eased towards the post, with all the runs since being in G1/G2 and close but no cigar. But returned from a break in May in a G1 and could be ready to strike again while back in listed company and getting Hollie back in the saddle.

This is Coltrane's easiest task for a very long time. His course and distance form here is second to none, and only Trawlerman, who is the current Ascot Gold Cup winner, was too good for him over course and distance in a Group 3 last time he ran here. The one to beat.

Getreadytorumble has hit form and won his last two races with ease. They were class 4 races, and clearly, he isn't class 4. The trainer is in form right now, so this step up to class 2 can be within his reach.
Was clearly thought highly of, being entered in a Group 2 at Royal Ascot last time out when being outclassed. Running well before that with form lines of 21. Go close.

Pearl Of Windsor can perhaps build on a strong fourth place in the Listed Scurry Stakes here last month, only beaten by less than two lengths. That was the three-year-old Pinatubo filly's best run for some time. Course and distance winner at age two. Trainer Conrad Allen's (SR 50%) last three runners have all won.

Previous course and distance winner Nad Alshiba Green won last time out at Nottingham. She doesn't look an obvious type to maybe follow up with a win as she steps up in grade, but the stable does well progressing horses, and she looks worth covering given her consistency.

Jungle Drums was a cracker last year with two C5 wins, which include winning on debut and a place and a win in listed company out of five runs. Although not great this year, the two runs so far have been big money events in Meydan, so worth an EW chance that he is ready for this return.

Two decent return runs from the 6yo mare this year, and her fitness should be spot on now. On a good mark, trip and going will suit her, and she has a strong jockey booking for this amateur riders’ handicap.

A 3-time career winner who has consistently been running well since last autumn, having won twice over a mile since then. The first was at Chelmsford in December and the last at Yarmouth in April. Finished well into 4th at Newmarket last time out 12 days ago and still looks fairly handicapped. Will likely finish as well as anything if the race is run at a fast pace.
Indian Springs won by 2 lengths a class 4 maiden at Newmarket back in april and he can win again in the same class this Novice Stakes.

This A M Balding-trained colt has finished runner-up in his last two races. The latest was over one mile four furlongs on good ground at Newbury 22 days ago when beaten 1 1/2 lengths behind the R Hughes-trained Circus Of Rome. So with Jason Watson back in the plate, he can break his duck tonight.

Three career runs for the 3yo colt, all on the AW. A near miss and a win in his last two starts. Excellent breeding and can prove to be much better on turf. Trained at a good yard. Plenty of improvement possible after 6 months off the track. Attractive mark in this low grade contest on his handicap debut. Good jockey booking.

Kentucky River comes from an impressive lineage. He has improving form and can handle different trips and terrains, and the trip should suit. I think this jockey can also bring out the best in him - trainer is (I think) underrated for the price here today, could go close.

Firmly at the bottom of the handicap mark in this field and did achieve first win at Lingfield back in May of this year and finished a credible 3rd of 6 in handicap debut LTO at Ripon last month. Mark remains unchanged but has a chance if improvements are made.
Has won just 1 of 8 starts but has placed twice, including when finishing 3rd on penultimate start. Holds an each-way chance if finding that form.

This Ian Williams-trained filly won for the first time on her penultimate start over one mile two furlongs on good to firm ground at Wetherby. She looked unlucky in her latest race over one mile two furlongs on good ground at Haydock when not getting a clear run behind a wall of horses when full of running, to be beaten four lengths behind the J Channon-trained Pomme Pomme. With P Mulrennan booked, she should go close to winning tonight.

Won here by nearly a length after three unsuccessful runs since debut. The step up in trip looked a positive move, and a further step up might not be a bad move here. Still looks quite progressive, and retains jockey here to try and make it two in two.

Jockey and trainer combination can never be ignored although not much sign of money so far. Relying on Marco Ghiani to get a better sound out of the filly; latest ride on her was a victory at Southwell. Jockey's last four rides for the stable have been 2211.

U Turn is an interesting runner here. The opening mark looks quite generous. Form figures of 322 in her last 3 runs, so she seems in good form and could do one better today in a generous handicap mark.

Land of Liberty could be an outsider to note with only 2 places on offer. David Menuisier's horses are going really well as of late as well. Hoping this one can outrun its odds and give us a run for our money.
Winner at Kempton in March. Has remained in decent form since both on the all weather and turf and wasn't beaten far in 5th at York last time. Should go well once again this evening.

Ran well on good/soft ground at Carlisle just 9 days ago. Victory at Nottingham (1m good) on June 1st highlights this horse's versatility. 2 wins from 6 starts this year (33% strike rate). Overall, 5 wins from 18, strong ROI on stakes bet, and again value for the price today.

BYZANTINE EMPRESS is back in Class 4 handicap company which should create a stronger pace for her to aim at with a field of deeper handicappers. She is a well treated sort who has drifted in the early markets possibly in the face of support for others , but the more relevant post-time market could tell us more.

STOCKPYLE has been performing pretty well since switching stables and has now undergone wind surgery to try and find further improvement. If that and the visor do the trick we could have one to break the duck for new connections. Not that impressive last time out but that was a tough looking handicap at York.

Going through a barren run as it's now been 11 runs since the last win, which was back in 2023. He really struggled LTO at Chester when he finished 13th of 13 last month, but he does have course experience. Hoping he can take advantage of the dropped mark.

There's plenty of rain in the forecast, and this is the last race on this evening card. Hopefully, the ground will have softened up by race time since I think that could be the key to this horse, which hasn't had his ground since he moved stables and has therefore slipped down the handicap, having shown next to nothing since the switch. His last run on soft was a winning one less than a year ago off a 2 lb higher mark, and he could well step up on those poor recent efforts here if the rain is sufficient enough. The trainer always has low strike rates, but the 2 wins and 2 places from his last 14 runners is way above his normal ratio, and this one could be worth a little bet in the e/w market.

There's a lot to like about the chances of Ventura Express in this sprint handicap. He likes Beverley, and has won this very race twice before. He has been running in higher class races most of the season where he has struggled against better horses. The stable have been in hot form this week, all pointing to a good show from the selection.

GOOD EARTH may need the splits at the right time , but no doubt he is quick enough feasibly treated and he deserves an upturn in fortune after his latest effort. He should appreciate Beverley's stiff five furlongs having run well at Sandown last time out and should be in the mix here.

Orbaan may be a ten year old now, but he's shown more than enough this season to think he will be more than good enough to win this seller. He's back up to a mile in this, which I believe is his best trip nowadays. He goes well at Beverley, and looks a good bet at the current price.

Mainly a hurdler but has got flat form, including 3 runs back when runner-up despite being a pound over and conceding first run. Has since won over hurdles off 106, so this mark of 54 means he is potentially a good few pounds well in.

Oscar's Sister, lightly raced for her age, goes to a course where past performances suggest she could go well with the right setup into the race. Very weak affair, and I think this one should win tomorrow.
Winning favourite here in mid-June despite having to take the race late after hitting traffic multiple times. Keeps a similar draw, retains jockey, and has gone up by only 2lbs for that victory.

Another that looks to have a bit of value is ELETTARIA. On better terms than Dumfries when she met some trouble in running. Could potentially go better on return here. Poor starts are the issue but not enough to dissuade as there's a good finish in the engine.
Beltane has been placed four times since the return in April and is still falling down the weights. Although not winning for a long time, when he did last win, it was here and worth an EW.

The stable has had a couple of winners these past few days. Comes here from a falling mark on the first run for 8 months. Ran much better than the bare result on his sole turf outing last year off 63, so is worth backing each way off 57 here.

The elder statesman in this field, but I'm happy to back when they seem to be running well, and RUM RUNNER ticks the box here. Nudged down in the weights after an improved run last time out and keeps the same claimer in the saddle. That was also the first run back after a lengthy time off, so if he progresses from a favorable stall position, there are each-way claims.
Soca Star sets the form standard here finishing 3rd in all three of their starts. Running anywhere close to that form should see them go close here today.
Found trouble in running last time out when could've gotten a lot closer. One to keep an eye on at bigger prices and top stable.

With 55 Mehmas offspring achieving victories on the flat, this filly has a bright future ahead, particularly with her Dam being a winner from 7f to 1m. Kevin Ryan's stable excels with debutants, so the 20/1 odds present a fantastic opportunity for an each-way wager.
Atmosphere looks the most likely winner here. Has escaped a penalty for the last time out win, and if they can act on the turf, then should be able to complete the double over the ideal trip.
Step up to a mile suited her when winning last time, having been beaten in photos the two races prior to that. Moves up another half furlong here. Should be more to come.

Four runner mares maiden hurdle at Bangor. Herja is the form choice. All 12 pro tipsters on the Racing Post card nominate the selection to win. Solid second of eight in a Class 4 maiden hurdle at this course last month. This looks an easier race. Brian Hughes (SR 23%) takes over jockey duties for Patrick Griffin. May offer a little value at odds of 1.83.

This could be another stamina test for Herja, and Dothejive got up on the line to dead heat in an Irish point in April before transferring to Jennie Candlish. She could be good enough to win in her first run under rules.
Won in a higher class/grade on penultimate start, but jumping let her down last time. If she can improve in the jumping department, she can win again here.
Leading player in recent form finished 2nd twice in a row. Longer trip should bring out further improvement and should be close at the finish again.

The model I run suggests an upset from Bahtiyar. This result has been driven by Bahtiyar having the highest RPR of this 6-horse race and an official ranking that leaves him lowest of the field. This subsequently means Bahtiyar goes out carrying significantly less weight than the others in the field. Steps out trying the cheek pieces for the first time to try and spark a bit of a revival. Prior form figures read 574-45 and needs to find something more to get over the line first. Murray Dodd on board relieves a further 3 lbs for claiming and takes the total weight differential to 1 stone 8 lbs over this 2m 7f trip. That's a sizeable weight difference over this distance and might well be telling by the end. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4. This has been driven by the small gap back to second in the race simulation.

Just 11 runs under rules for the 8yo. A big improvement this year after joining a new yard. Two wins and a one length defeat over fences in his three runs - big RPR ratings in his last two runs. Now switching to hurdles but his mark is 10lb lower than his chase mark.

The model I run suggests Guillaume can win this one. Guillaume lines up here with the highest RPR in this 7-horse race but has an official ranking that is second lowest in the field. This subsequently means Guillaume goes out carrying 7 lbs less than the current market leader and over 20 lbs less than the top weight. Comes here with some reasonable form on offer with figures of 944-26, with that last effort coming only 28 days ago, so race fitness shouldn't be a concern. The model has issued a 'low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Only 8th of 12 on latest outing at Aintree but did win at Hereford on penultimate start. Each way chance if rediscovering that form.
Hasn't been in form lately but this looks like a race where they could make all the running unlike previous runs. Could easily be thrown in here on old chase form. Looks to outrun the odds here.

Never Seen Again, a 7-year-old who has not had much racing, has been gently reintroduced by a new trainer. Done well on all three starts, and had he settled better, he could have been closer last time. He will be asked to give it all today and could be enough to get the yard's first winner. A sharp 2m on quick ground looks sure to suit this Epaulette gelding with a mostly speedy, flat pedigree.

I tipped Land Girls Luck the last twice she has won, and I'm tipping her again to get her hat-trick. I don't think the handicapper has caught up with her yet and there is every chance she could go in again.

The model I run suggests Mrs. Tabitha can win this one. Mrs. Tabitha lines up here with the highest RPR of this 6-horse field but has an official ranking that is the lowest. This subsequently means Mrs. Tabitha goes out carrying less weight than the other runners here. The weight gap from Mrs. Tabitha to the market leader is over 1 stone over this 2m 3f trip. Form figures of 292-35 and prior course winner, so looking for some improvement to get back into form. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests Donald Jump can win this one. Donald Jump lines up here with the highest RPR of the 6 horse field and isn't overly penalised for it in the weights. There is a very small weight difference across all horses here top to bottom. Donald Jump came 3rd in his only race 13 days ago and will come on bags from that experience. Lots of unknown types in here who haven't run a race before. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Showed plenty of promise when finishing 3rd at Southwell on debut in May. Should improve for having had that run and likely to be there or thereabouts.
Twice a winner over fences last year and has been in good form over hurdles of late, finishing 2nd here before winning over this course and distance last time. Should be there or thereabouts.

The model I run suggests an upset from Wudya. This result has been driven by Wudya having the highest RPR of the 6 runners here but an official ranking that leaves Wudya second last in the rankings. This means Wudya goes out carrying significantly less weight than the other runners here. Peter Kavanagh on board relieves a further 3 lbs for claiming, which takes the total weight differential to the top weight to over 1 stone over this 2m 3f trip. Wudya had form figures of 5172-P, so can clearly go close on the day, just a bit unreliable. 29s looks overpriced and represents good value here for the win probability %. The model has issued a 'low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

This 5-year-old placed in 2 points. He achieved 2nd place in a novice hurdle at Ballinrobe on his NH debut 38 days ago, clear ahead of the rest. Under the Elliott yard's training, he looks set to advance and is predicted to perform admirably over a longer distance.

The model I run suggests The Man's Room can win this one. The Man's Room has the highest RPR of this larger 14-runner field and is not penalized for it in the weights. Has shown some decent form coming into this with figures of 55-2 and looks to be progressing nicely. Last out 36 days ago, so race fitness shouldn't be a concern. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator driven by the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Quarry Tiepy could have needed her first run over hurdles after a break of over two and a half years since she won in a point and Paul Townend rides her this time.

A 6-year-old with great promise, but has yet to win after 8 hurdle races. He secured a good 2nd place in a handicap hurdle at Punchestown 26 days ago, just missing out on the win. Form claims are impressive.
Has run well over hurdles, and every run has indicated he needs further. Gets the furthest he has gone so far today and sure to suit. Kennedy is back, which is great, and must go close.

The model I run suggests Coumeenoole can win this one. Coumeenoole lines up here with a comparably high RPR to the other 13 runners in the field but doesn't look overly penalized for it in the weights. Only carries 7 lbs more than the lowest weight running. In terms of closest competition based on market pricing, Coumeenoole carries 8 lbs less around this 3m trip. Needs to run well fresh having not run in a significant length of time, but hopefully the time off has done some good. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
May Call You Back was eased before the finish when following up with her second win last time and she should be able to cope with another seven pounds penalty.
Burru holds every chance here. Strong claims now back down in trip after just being outstayed on return run finishing 2nd. Still looks on handy mark on hurdle form. Should go close again.

Crowsatedaappletart last won at Cork over hurdles back on December 24 but has been consistent since, being placed in all 6 starts. He was 3rd, beaten 5 lengths behind May Call You Back at Tipperary on Tuesday. Although unlikely to turn the tables with that one, he again looks like a good EW bet with 5 places on offer.

The model I run suggests Roman Parish can win this one. Roman Parish lines up here with a comparably high RPR to the other 15 runners here but has an official ranking that is the second lowest. This means Roman Parish goes out carrying the second lowest amount of weight around this 2m 3f round trip. Second place finish last time out 34 days ago and looks to press on with race fitness under the belt. The model has issued a 'very low' stakes indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

James Barcoe's 10 year old Gelding EARLY ARRIVAL is relatively lightly tried over the tall timber well atleast if you measure it against his hurdle experience & 'could' be a danger off his lower Chase mark of 82 & considering this Son of RULE OF LAW hadn't jumped over fences since 2023 AND was returning from a 217 day sabbatical at Tramore 34 days ago the 3rd place looks very good & if you factor in that horses he had in behind him were both pipped in 2nd place since it doesn't paint a bad picture. This drop back in trip shouldn't break this lad out into sweats, he has won twice (& placed 6 times) over 20f (albeit over the smaller obstacles). Jockey Patrick O'Brien gets the leg up & sheds 7lbs & has a 28.57% place strike rate here (past 5 years). Look it's risky BUT should this charge kick on now fresh back over a trip he relishes then he certainly wouldn't be a forlorn hope to atleast hit the frame.

Won a maiden hurdle last time out, so can easily be thrown in on that form. Has been steadily progressive of late, and the longer trip looks to suit on the return to the flat after that last performance, running out an easy winner by 3 lengths. One to watch closely.

Lohengrin is still a maiden after 18 starts, but he has been placed 6 times. He was 3rd last month at Limerick off a mark of 57. He makes his debut here for John Ryan, and if he can find any improvement, he looks like a good each-way bet with 4 places on offer.
Has not been seen since September 2023 but was a 3-time winner when trained in France and has placed in 2 of the last 3 outings. Each way chance if retaining that ability.

This horse races from out of the handicap, but he did last time as well and showed some improvement for the step up to 9f, making some good late headway. That leads me to believe that this lightly raced type will improve again today in this similar type of handicap, stepping up to 12f. He has lots of scope if the increased distance proves to be suitable, and the stable has hit a bit of form recently.

EASTMORE could be one trainer Charles Byrnes has set aside to land some bets. This is a modest looking handicap and the last time the money was down he was narrowly denied. Maybe the market will again be the best guide for us today.

The model I run suggests Phoenix Cowboy can win this one. Phoenix Cowboy lines up with the highest RPR of this larger 14-horse race but is not penalized for it in the weights. Steps out carrying a similar weight load to the others around him in the market. Consistent running figures of 435-436 but needs to show some improvement now to get over the line first in this one. Darragh O'Keeffe picks up the reins, who's a trusted pair of hands. Last out 36 days ago, so race fitness shouldn't be a concern. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Liam Cusack's 5-year-old gelding HIGHLAND EARL has yet to shed his maiden tag, but he certainly took a step in the right direction 36 days ago at Limerick (19f Good) when looking to throw down a challenge 3 from the lollipop but faded. So the step back in trip on that basis alone looks positive. This son of HIGHLAND REEL drops 1lb and retains the services of jockey Brian Hayes, which is another plus with the rider in decent form currently with a 50% place strike rate the past month. Trainer Cusack also has some interesting stats with a respectable 37.50% here at Wexford the past 5 years. At current 14/1 odds, there is enough here for me to side with this lad in the hopes he takes another progressive step forward.

The model I run suggests Menas Miracle can win this one. Menas Miracle lines up here with a comparably high RPR to the other 13 runners in the field but has an official ranking that leaves her well treated. Steps out carrying 1 stone 7 lbs less of initial weight to the top weight and current market leader Hatfield Hammer.Conor Stone-Walsh on board relieves a further 3 lbs which helps. That could be telling over this 2m 1f round trip. Menas Miracle came second last time out 35 days ago and looks to make some improvement to get over the line first. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Although still a maiden after 31 starts, Ballycommon Chapel can go well here. She has been placed on 4 occasions and has been running well this year. She was second of 16 at Tipperary in May before finishing 4th over course and distance here two weeks later. She was brought down at the 4th flight at Sligo last month when backed into favourite. Off the same mark, she looks a big price and a good each-way bet with 4 places on offer.

I may well be seeing things that aren't there (it wouldn't be the first time!!) but im willing to take a small punt on Eoin Doyle's 7 year old Mare SPECIAL PROTECTOR, Now I know this Daughter of THE GURKHA is 0-11 over hurdles but in all honesty this charges run here 37 days ago wasn't awful (finished 7th of 21) considering she was returning from a 250 day break & continues to drop down the weights shedding an extra 2lbs here aswell as getting another 7lbs from today's rider 'Baby Shark' Paddy Hanlon who found himself In the winners enclosure 4 days ago & has a 19.23% place strike rate here the past 5 years. It could be something it could be nothing but at 28/1 I'm happy to ride the potential upward curve.

The model I run suggests Harsh can win this one. Harsh lines up here with by far the highest RPR of the 7-runner field and is not penalized for it in the weights. All horses go out carrying the same initial amount of weight. Came third last time out 18 days ago and looks to use that race fitness to get over the line first. Gordon Elliot-trained horse is the youngest here and looks to be the most progressive. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Consistent Sort won over further, so the trip shouldn't be a problem. Gets a good draw and the ground should suit. Will leave it late to strike and looks well in at weights.

6-year-old Mare. C&D champion. Placed 7th in a handicap at Leopardstown 15 days ago, not ideally situated. The 5 time winner, who triumphed in this race last year, may need to settle for a runner-up position this time, but is likely to provide an each-way profit at 16/1.

Worth an each-way bet. Shaped well on debut last time, doing best of those held up. Should improve for the run, but I just fear this step up in trip may not see this speed-bred gelding at his best. Could be a handicap project.

Carwyn is a lightly raced two year old colt by Masar, set for his first out today. With no prior form, this is a true debut, which can lead to inflated market odds on a good proposition. Lyons is a top Irish handler and the colt's pedigree suggests quality and an interesting value bet.

North Moon is a 5-year-old son of Spanish Moon ex North Face and is thus a half-brother to Ruffles Face by Authorized. He makes his racecourse debut in this 2m bumper where he'll be ridden by Mr. P.W. Mullins for his father W.P. Mullins. He's one for your horse tracker. The stable is in top form at the moment. I make him my Nap of the day.

The model I run suggests Ozarks Walk can win this one. Ozarks Walk lines up here with the highest RPR of this inexperienced lineup. All horses go out carrying the same initial amount of weight. Claiming jockey on board relieves 7 lbs, which helps. Second place finish last time out 33 days ago and looks to go one better here today. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Disappointed on debut in August last year when only 7th of 11, but is bred to be better than that. Any improvement will give an each-way chance.

MONEY SHUFFLER has Harry Swan booked who must be one of the best jockeys in this field especially in races of this nature. This mare is turned around relatively quickly for an out-of-season Bumper and that could be telling us she has improved significantly on the back of her debut effort.

This looks like being a competitive race, and there are a few with good chances. I am going to back My Girl Sioux to win it, who has been consistently going close, including a place over course and distance.
Placed in both her starts and improved between starts. Probably beaten by a decent one last time. More improvement to come and the right favorite here.

The model I run suggests Clarens can win this one. Clarens lines up here with a comparably high RPR in what looks like a tightly bunched group on paper. Clarens has an official ranking that leaves it looking well treated off this mark and goes out carrying a relatively low amount of weight compared to some of the other runners. Good win when last out 35 days ago and will need to find a bit more to get it done here today. Prior course winner so clearly likes this track. From figures of 571-31. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Nt Field Minnesota could have needed her run at Kilbeggan when 3rd, beaten three lengths by Shes A Fine Wine. Although running two pounds out of the handicap here, she is three pounds better off with the De Bromhead mare and could get her revenge.
Three times hurdles winner who has taken to chasing and won 2 of the last 3 races. Raised 9 lbs, but that is likely to be manageable. Holds at least an each-way chance.

THINK ABOUT IT is a Johnny Murtagh trained potential improver and she has a sound sire. She also gets to take her chance from a now career-low mark in a weak looking handicap and so with the stable and jockey easing into form she should show up well.

Looks to me like this one's been plotted for this handicap. Ran an eye-catching race on debut but had failed to progress from that. But I think this track will suit, and it's a very, very open race. I think the top of the market is worth taking on.

C&D Victor. Her latest triumph occurred here in April. She placed 15th in a handicap at Leopardstown 29 days ago. The visor is reattached. Presently in reserve, she can deliver a strong performance and vie for the runner-up spots if she gets a chance to race. An each-way wager at 18/1 appears to be a worthwhile investment.

Returning from a long absence last time on stable debut, this horse met soft going conditions and may have been inconvenienced by that, as well as struggling for race fitness. Will improve for that and showed plenty enough when based in the UK to suggest he can win a low-grade handicap like this, especially in the hands of J C McConnell.
